sheet.title: Happy Thanksgiving from Brennan’s, 3 Courses $80: choice of appetizer, entrée and dessert
sheet.line: Potato and Leek Écrasé, Brown Butter, Lemon, Capers
sheet.note: The sheet prints the dish name and its line and nothing else: no allergen marks, no price of its own (the $80 covers three courses), no method, no portion, no wine.

classic.meuniere: À la meunière, in the style of the miller’s wife, is the French way of dredging fish in flour and cooking it in butter, finished with brown butter, lemon and parsley; the flour is the usual reason given for the name (Wikipedia, Meunière sauce; Tasting Table, A La Meunière; CooksInfo, A la Meunière). Trout meunière is a bedrock dish of New Orleans Creole cooking (Wikipedia, Meunière sauce, citing the Gulf’s seafood). When the style came to New Orleans is not documented.
classic.ecrase: Écrasé is French for crushed: an écrasé de pommes de terre is potatoes crushed with a fork or a masher with olive oil or butter, rougher than a purée and made without milk (Bonial, pommes de terre écrasées à l’huile d’olive; Cookidoo, Écrasé de pomme de terre; Slate, the fork test). The sheet adds leeks; the pack’s leek component explains them.

unsourced: Whether the kitchen dredges the redfish in flour, where the fish comes from, and how the écrasé is finished: asked of the chef.
When meunière reached New Orleans: not documented.
